description: Meta in Record: the same helper and conversation panel as in Baude (Meta.panel.json describes the shared part: box, replies, tool cards, settings changes, undo, Changelog). This file lists only where Record's differs: it works on notebooks and pages, takes quoted passages, proposes edits to pages, and has no sessions or tabs of its own. One conversation for the whole window, whichever notebook is open (kept in the notebooks' file).

parts.name: page switcher
parts.shows: At the top of the right column: Meta, Files, Git. (Baude's right column has more.) Files and Git are of the folder of the chat being read; with no chat read they have no folder.

parts.name: what Meta works on
parts.shows: Meta reads the open notebook's pages and folders, and what is @-referenced in what you ask (a page, a notebook, a file, a chat: its text goes with the message). Its first message of a session says which notebook is open, or which notebooks there are with none open; it is told again when another notebook is opened. It knows where you are as "host / notebook / page". Each of your messages remembers the notebook it was asked in (a restarted session's earlier conversation says "[in {notebook}] " or "[no notebook open] ").

decisions.said: Drop the hamstrung Record agent: it should be a regular agent; @ references (notebooks and pages too) in its box, the agent sees what is referenced, and it can propose diffs in Record (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Meta in every app that has notebooks takes @ references to notebooks, pages, files and chats in its box, sends their text with the message, and proposes changes to pages as tracked edits the user accepts or rejects.

decisions.said: Switching notebooks switched Meta agents, a holdover from the notebook-bound Record agent; Meta is window-bound, so remove the coupling.
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta has one conversation per window, whichever notebook is open; opening another notebook tells it, and doesn't start another.

parts.name: quote chip
parts.shows: Over the box you type in, while a passage is quoted: a quote-styled box of up to 3 lines (ends in …) and at its right a flat × button, tooltip "Drop the passage". A passage selected on a page shows "{page} · {text}"; picked in a chat read shows the text, several as "[1] … [2] …". At most 6000 characters. The quote goes with what you ask; a change proposed to a selected passage replaces it. Leaving for another notebook lets go of a quote of the notebook left. What was typed (the quote too) is kept with a restart.

actions.does: Drops the quote and puts the focus back in the box.
A quote alone can be sent (an empty question asks about the passage).

decisions.said: The selected-text box in Record's Meta was ugly: it should look as it does once sent, above the prompt inside the box, bar in the accent cap colour, an X at its right, square corners.
decisions.rule: Every app shows a quoted passage over the text inside the box, drawn as the sent message's quote is (a rule at its left, here in the accent), with a square × button at its right to drop it; the box grows to hold it.

parts.name: sent bubble's quote
parts.shows: Your sent message shows its quote as a chip above the text; for a page's passage it begins "{page} · ".

parts.name: pending edits bar
parts.shows: Over the box, only while the open notebook has proposed edits waiting: "{n} edit pending" / "{n} edits pending" at the left and two flat round buttons, up (tooltip "Previous edit") and down ("Next edit").

actions.does: Goes to the edit before or after the one last gone to (wrapping round): opens its page, shows the edit there, scrolled to, the caret in it (Tab takes it, Esc leaves it).

parts.name: edit card
parts.shows: A tool card in a reply for propose_edit, revise_edit and edit_page: the short page name as its summary, the passage it replaces (old) and what it puts in (new) as the hunks, and a slot at the end of its line: for an edit waiting here, a tick button (tooltip "Accept") and a cross (tooltip "Reject"); otherwise dim text saying what became of it: "accepted", "rejected", "taken back", "revised" (a later call changed it; that call's card has it as it is), "waiting in {notebook}" with an "Open" button (tooltip "Open {notebook}"), "waiting in a notebook that's gone", or "its page is gone" with a cross only (tooltip "Reject (its page is gone)"). A hunk is dimmed unless the edit is in the page.

actions.does: Opens the page, shows the edit and accepts it, as the page's own Accept does.
Opens that notebook and shows the edit on its page, the caret in it.

decisions.said: Proposed and revised edits should look like diff hunks; they looked like generic tool calls.
decisions.rule: Every app draws a proposed, revised or made edit to a page as a hunk: the text it replaces on red, what it puts in on green, under the page's name.

parts.name: edit-only reply
parts.shows: A reply that did nothing but edit and has no text (from before tool cards) says "Edited {pages}" and/or "Took back an edit to {pages}" in a dimmed small line.

parts.name: tool card summaries
parts.shows: add_page, delete_page, edit_page: the page's short name. move_pages: "{pages} → {parent or 'the top'}" with " (from {notebook})" and " (into {notebook})" when across notebooks. add_notebook: its name. Deleting says "Deleted {what}". A card for edit_page has a link to its page (marked in the Pages list).

parts.name: Not in your notes chips
parts.shows: Under a reply that explained a chat's passage and ended with an "Unknown: …" line (that line is not shown): a flow of "Not in your notes:" then a chip per name, "+ {term}" (tooltip "Add to To learn") or "✓ {term}" and disabled when the notebook's notes already mention it. Only while the notebook it was asked in is open.

actions.does: Adds the term to the To learn list on Home (a toast "“{term}” added to To learn" with an "Open" button that opens Home) and the chip becomes ✓.

parts.name: names in replies
parts.shows: Names of the notebooks, pages, chats and of the chat read's folder in a reply are links with logos, and resting on one shows its card with a "To notes" button; a click opens it where it is (as in a chat read).

parts.name: marks in lists
parts.shows: Things Meta added, deleted, moved or highlighted show in the notebooks' list, the Pages list and open pages as Meta's marks (green for added or edited, struck through for deleted) until you keep or undo them; clicking a change's page opens it (a deleted one: read-only tab "{page} (deleted)").

parts.name: forms and buttons
parts.shows: Meta can show a "New page" form in a reply: a text box (placeholder "Its name"), an "Under" choice ("(the top)" or a page of the notebook, Home first), and a multi-line box for its Markdown text; its button "Add" makes the page and says "made {page}"; with no name or a name taken it says why instead: "A page needs a name" or "There's a page {name} already". Meta can also show a red "Delete {notebook}…" button (opens the delete dialog, RecordAlerts) and a blue "Open {host}" button (switches the notebooks' host).

parts.name: settings Meta can change
parts.shows: Those Baude's has in common (Accent Colour, Code Font, Text/Icon/Global Scale, Full-width text, Auto restart on update, Notifications) and Record's own: Markup visibility and Include glossary and chats in backup. Asked about a setting, it shows that setting's row, the same row as Settings has.

states.name: no notebook open
states.shows: Meta works, but a tool that works on the open notebook says "No notebook is open: add_page takes notebook, move_pages from_notebook and to_notebook, and add_notebook makes one."

decisions.said: Meta in Record should work with no notebook set up and be able to make notebooks; notebooks should behave more like pages, so pages can be moved into a new one.
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta works with no notebook open, can make a notebook, and can move pages between notebooks as one change.
